summary: Prototype 1946 Flattop Mountain cab, dismantled and moved to the Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center in Entiat; sources disagree on the move date and on whether it is a replica.

facts.design: Prototype two-story frame cab with slanted windows and curved hip roof, built 1946; sources give 14x14 ft (WillhiteWeb, FireLookout.com) or 12x12 ft (NHLR)
facts.status_note: Original cab dismantled and moved to CBFIC in Entiat; the Entiat structure is a rebuild with some original wood, which SummitPost and WillhiteWeb call a replica and which is one story rather than two

staffing.status: Mr. and Mrs. Ernest Fiedler named as lookouts in 1952, then Forest Couch for the rest of that fire season; summit abandoned 1960

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (original cab); Columbia Breaks Fire Interpretive Center (current site)

access.note: CBFIC is a public fire interpretive center at 15212 Highway 97A, Entiat (CBFIC page; SummitPost). No source read says whether the rebuilt cab can be entered.

visit.trail_note: Interpretive trails and signs on the CBFIC site (SummitPost)

events.note: Prototype two-story cab built for the Forest Service by the Alladin Company of Portland, Oregon (WillhiteWeb)
Mr. and Mrs. Ernest Fiedler named as lookouts; they went to teaching jobs when school started, and Forest Couch took over for the rest of the season
Forest Fire Lookout Association dismantled the east cab and moved it to CBFIC in Entiat, per FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb. The Former Fire Lookout Sites register instead says disassembled by 2025
NHLR visit report dated May 15, 2005: building neglected, hole in the roof, several stair steps missing
Reconstruction at CBFIC began October 2009 and was completed in spring 2010 as a one-story building (SummitPost gives both dates)
Former Fire Lookout Sites register lists the original tower as removed by 2025 and disassembled

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb date the FFLA dismantling and move to 2005. The Former Fire Lookout Sites register says the tower was disassembled by 2025. SummitPost dates reconstruction at CBFIC to October 2009 through spring 2010. The story gives each date with its source and does not choose one.
FireLookout.com and WillhiteWeb give 14x14 feet; the NHLR gives 12x12 feet. The story reports both.
SummitPost reports that some people consider the Entiat cab an original moved lookout, while CBFIC and many others call it a replica. The story reports the dispute rather than choosing a side.

The brief's OpenStreetMap record marks the site standing; that OSM entry was not read. The original cab is no longer on the summit (Former Fire Lookout Sites register), so relocated fits the original; the surviving Entiat structure is a rebuild.
The CBFIC address is Highway 97A; WillhiteWeb places the center on US Highway 97. The story gives the address from the center's own page.

notes_for_editor: Dates and replica status conflict across sources and the story says so. The FFLOS 'disassembled by 2025' and SummitPost's 2009-2010 rebuild cannot both be read as the only move date; the brief's relocated event has no year. The summit's current condition is not described by any source read. The CBFIC access level is inferred from its public-center description; no source says whether the cab can be entered. Source spelling 'Alladin' kept as printed. No new photos recorded. One WebSearch found a FFLA member account saying the Entiat cab is not a replica, but that page was not fetched or quoted, so it is not used.
